text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The International Monetary Fund approved a $430 million loan for Romania.
- Floods affected scores of households in central Romania.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The tourism ministry plans to privatise 53 companies in in the sector.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's President met the troops to be sent to Albania to participate in the international pacekeeping force.
- A parliamentary commission ended its report on Romanian Inteligence Service (SRI) 1996 activity, the paper says.
- The newspaper reports on floods which affected nine counties.
- In the northern county of Salaj a dysentery epidemic was reported. A total of 156 cases have been reported.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The head of Romania's Foreign Intelligence Service (SIE) will advise the General Prosecutor about alleged illegal leaking of information by two officers.
- German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel is to start a two-day visit to Romania on April 30.
ADEVARUL
- A 52-year-old man in a coma was left to die on the street by an ambulance crew after hospitals refused to accept him.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romanian police found seven kg of heroin hidden in television sets coming from Pakistan. The drugs were to be sold in Italy.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
